channel.title: Muntin Digital — restaurant web library
channel.description: Articles, glossary, and tools for independent restaurants — written and maintained by Don Goldstein.

item.title: 30 days after leaving DoorDash: a restaurant operator's case study
item.description: The first 30 days after delisting a restaurant from DoorDash have a predictable shape. The playbook: what to expect each week, which costs flex, which complaints arrive, and what the channel mix usually does. Illustrative ranges anchored to the DoorDash margin walk.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: How to get your restaurant cited in Google's AI Overviews
item.description: The search result is a paragraph Google wrote, citing two or three sources. Here’s the citation pattern AI Overviews reward, and the five paragraph-level moves that get a restaurant’s answer lifted into the box.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: How to respond to Google reviews: a restaurant operator's playbook
item.description: Four review archetypes — the glowing 5-star, the disappointed 3-star, the angry 1-star, and the legitimate-complaint 2-star. The response template for each, what to never write, and how the response itself becomes a search-result surface.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: Instagram as restaurant SEO: stop posting, start indexing
item.description: Instagram is a search engine now. Google has indexed it since 2024 and the in-app search bar accounts for a meaningful share of restaurant discovery for younger guests. Almost no independent restaurant treats it like an SEO surface. Here’s what the indexable post looks like.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: Loyalty programs for independent restaurants: what works, what doesn't, what they cost
item.description: Punch cards, Toast/Square Loyalty, Square Marketing, Fivestars, the standalone Slice/ChowNow rewards stack — what the four main loyalty models actually cost, what they actually return, and which one to skip if you only have time for one.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: The May 2026 wave: nine pieces, one operating thesis
item.description: An overview of the nine new pieces in the May 2026 publication batch — AI Overview citation, schema markup, Google Maps invisibility, review responses, Instagram as SEO, three-platform delivery math, the 30-day case study, loyalty programs, and service charges vs tipping. The through-line, the data behind each, and the order to read them in.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: My restaurant isn't on Google Maps: the 10-minute diagnostic
item.description: Four causes account for the bulk of restaurant map-pack invisibility: unclaimed Google Business Profile, wrong primary category, suspended listing, and duplicate listing. Walk through the diagnostic and the fix for each, in 10 minutes flat.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: Restaurant schema markup: a complete, paste-ready example
item.description: The full JSON-LD block I use on real restaurant sites — Restaurant, Menu, OpeningHoursSpecification, AggregateRating, Reservation, and FAQ in one file. Drop it into your <head>, fill in seven fields, validate, ship. Worked example from a live DMV restaurant.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: Service charges vs tipping: the operator's math for 2026
item.description: The DMV is mid-transition. Some restaurants are 20% service charge in-house, some are still tipping, some are a hybrid. The take-home for the server, the cost structure for the operator, and the customer-perception swing — on paper, with the actual numbers.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: Uber Eats vs DoorDash vs Grubhub: the honest math for independent restaurants, 2026
item.description: Three platforms, the same $42 ticket, the same line items. Side-by-side margin walks, the marketing-fee trap nobody talks about, and the platform you can almost always drop without losing a customer.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: Should Your Restaurant Actually Make an App in 2026?
item.description: Every month a new agency pitches an independent restaurant a $20K app. Here's the honest answer to whether you need one — and the three cheaper tools that deliver what you actually wanted the app to do.
item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: Toast vs. Square vs. Clover: Which POS Integrates Best With a Restaurant Website?

item.dc:creator: Don Goldstein

item.title: An honest DoorDash math for independent restaurants, 2026

item.title: How to Tell If a Restaurant Tool Is Safe (Before You Type a Real Number)
item.description: A 5-test framework you can run on any free restaurant tool — in your browser, in under a minute — before you type a single real number into it. Plus the 4-tier data model that tells you what to share, where, and the worked example of what 'safe' looks like in practice.

item.title: Restaurant Schema Markup: The 6 Types Google Actually Uses

item.title: When to Rebuild Your Restaurant Website: A Decision Framework
item.description: Most operators rebuild their restaurant website 18 months too late. This is the seven-question decision framework I run through with every studio client — and the three case threads that show what each answer actually changes.

item.title: Can ChatGPT Write Your Restaurant Website? (And Should It?)
item.description: An honest look at what AI can and can't write for an independent restaurant website. The specific places ChatGPT gets it wrong, the places it can save you real time, and the one-page formula that makes the output actually sound like your restaurant.
